<margin>Commentary by Su</margin>
If one studies without knowing the Way, knowledge and sight increase daily, but there is no way to unify them; this inevitably leads to a burden. Confucius said, "When hearing much, select the good and follow it; when seeing much, remember it. This is the second level of knowledge." If one truly knows the Way, one looks at falsehood as false. If one acts, it is not without a single thought of deception. Removing deception and returning to one's nature is what is meant by "decrease." When someone asked Confucius, "Do you consider me one who learns much and remembers it?" he replied, "Yes, is it not so?" Confucius said, "No. I unify it with one thread." To forget the heart in order to return purely to one's nature is "decrease." If one does not stop at forgetting the heart and returning to one's nature, but proceeds to forget even this, then the heart is pure and the nature is restored without remainder. Then, one removes the "acting," and one does not fail to reach "non-action." People all have desires to take hold of the world and the reasoning of things. Thus, they create affairs and seek them. When the heart manifests externally, things resent it; thus, it is difficult and cannot be attained. The sage practices non-action; thus, there are no affairs. When his heart manifests externally, things are at peace. Even if he does not take hold of the world and its reasoning, and yet handles them, the reasoning of the world is then compliant and peaceful.

<margin>Commentary by Lü</margin>
Learning is for those who have not yet heard of the Way. Because those who have not heard of the Way seek it, they cannot help but be extensive; hence, it is said, "Increase." Practicing the Way is for those who have already heard of the Way. Because those who have already heard of the Way practice it, they cannot help but be in non-action; hence, it is said, "Decrease." To say "decrease and decrease again" means one has not yet avoided having action. To reach the point of forgetting even the act of decreasing, one arrives at non-action. Non-action means to be silent and unmoving. "Nothing left undone" means to respond and penetrate the causes of the world. To be in non-action and arrive at the ultimate non-action is what is called "the constant." If study has no worry, it is called spirit. The function of spirit is what is called the Way. Who can participate in this ultimate spirit? Looking at it this way, one knows that to take the world, one must always use non-action. If one uses action, one is not enough to take the world.

<column-break/>

<margin>Commentary by Huang Maocai</margin>
Only when there is nothing one does not know can one speak of learning; thus, learning wishes to increase daily. Only when there is nothing one does not do can one speak of the Way; thus, the Way wishes to decrease daily. However, "increase" can be pursued through advancement, while "decrease" is perhaps difficult to force. Only the extremely bright can suddenly cast off their attachments and arrive at the ground of non-action. Thus, they can do nothing that is not done, and their application in the world is inexhaustible and abundant.

<margin>Commentary by Xizhai</margin>
Learning is the means to seek knowledge; thus, it increases daily. Practicing the Way is the means to remove deception; thus, it decreases daily. If knowledge is not extreme, the decrease is not complete; thus, "increasing daily" is the ground for "decreasing daily." If one decreases and decreases again, deception is removed and the true is complete, then there is non-action. Once one reaches non-action, whatever is done is never "not-non-action." This is not something that can be easily discussed in terms of increase or decrease. When one arrives at the ultimate non-action, even though the world is vast, one unifies it with a single thread. If one creates affairs where there are none, one is hard-pressed. If even a single thing from before is still tangled and erroneous, how much more so for the multitude of things in the world?

The sage has no constant heart. He takes the heart of the common people as his heart. To those who are good, I am good; to those who are not good, I am also good, so that virtue becomes good. To those who are trustworthy, I am trustworthy; to those who are not trustworthy, I am also trustworthy, so that virtue becomes trustworthy. <summary>This page explores the transition from the accumulation of knowledge (increasing) to the shedding of attachments (decreasing) as the path to non-action, emphasizing that the sage harmonizes with the world by aligning his heart with the hearts of the people.</summary>
